evaluation_protocol: Read this file before proposing each trial. State which requirements the change targets and which previously working features it could harm.
Freeze parameters, seed, source hashes, native buffers and cameras. Keep the rejected baseline available.
Use close, wide, whole-canopy and oblique native renders. Compare finished reference pixels; construction supports alone are insufficient for a star-stage match.
Hold camera, crop, display size and exposure fixed between candidates. Record any later camera-calibration change separately and apply it to all compared candidates.
Write a per-candidate verdict for every D and V requirement: pass, partial, fail or not_evaluated, with evidence and a reason. No missing requirements and no automatic pass from an unrelated metric.

Inspect for new discrepancies after every comparison. Add a new requirement or refine an existing one without deleting old requirements; record its source and whether it is a user instruction or assistant observation.
Do not promote a candidate merely because it improves the newest complaint. Regressions in dense regions, connections, curve readability or another earlier requirement keep it a diagnostic trial.
Tests verify mechanics, not screenshot resemblance. Unknown reference camera/geometry is a limitation to address, not a reason to label a visibly poor match acceptable.

Explain what placement can fix, what requires scaffold changes and what requires rendering changes. Continue authorized work; do not wait for unrequested confirmation or stop without explaining remaining failures.
standing_workflow: Core instruction: always explain what you did, in plain language in every substantive work report. Read and follow the core reporting section at the top of AGENTS.md; links and experiment names do not replace the explanation.
Read AGENTS.md and README.md before project changes.
Do not overwrite live config/plot.json or config/controls.ini, stop the viewer, or launch it automatically.
Keep native Windows/OpenGL workflow and avoid unnecessary dependency changes.
Keep math separate from rendering, reuse shared population/postprocessing, explain control units/randomness/count effects.
Preserve the accepted shared lighting formula and previous experiments.
